Nx Cloud Public API

This is an API reference of the Nx Cloud Public API. View OpenAPI specification

Read-only access to Nx Cloud CI data: CI pipeline executions (CIPEs), run groups, runs, tasks, workflows, steps, instances, agents, daily task statistics, flaky-task metrics, and Self-Healing CI fixes.

Navigation: each response has a links map. Follow the links to reach the entity’s parents and children. A child link is a pre-filled filter URL (a run group’s runs link is /runs?runGroup={id}). Start from /cipes, or from any entity URL you have. Use the top-level collections to search the workspace. Use the parent-id filters (cipeId, runGroup, stepId, agentName) to list one parent’s children. A parent-id filter is an address: an unknown parent gives 404, never an empty page.

In-progress entities: CIPEs and run groups are listed while they run, with fields that are not final yet absent. Their children are reached one level down: a running CIPE’s run groups at its links.runGroups, a running run group’s finished runs at its links.runs. Fetching a running CIPE or run group by id gives 409 not_terminal with the same links. Runs and tasks are never listed in progress: a run appears in the run lists once its Nx command finishes. Fetching a live run, or a task of one, by id gives 409 not_terminal with no links. Steps, instances and agents are served once their run group and its workflow finish.

Requests: every endpoint is a GET. Each entity has its own path version (/nx-cloud/data/{version}/{entity}). Repeat a key for list filters (statuses=FAILED&statuses=CANCELED). Enum values are not case-sensitive. An unknown query param gives 400 invalid_parameter. Ids are raw: URL-encode them in a path. Terminal timestamps are completedAt.

Authentication: choose one credential set. Send a CI access token in Authorization: Bearer <token>. Or send a personal access token (PAT) in Nx-Cloud-Personal-Access-Token: <token> together with Nx-Cloud-Id: <id>. The Nx Cloud Id identifies the workspace. Only the PAT option requires both headers. The nx-cloud api command authenticates for you with the login nx login stores. OAuth login is the default CLI credential when it is enabled on the instance; otherwise nx login uses a PAT. PATs remain supported.

Pagination: limit (1..500, default 100), sort (ASC or DESC, default DESC), and cursor. A cursor is opaque and stays valid only for the list that minted it. Filters do not change that scope. sort applies to the first request only: a cursor carries its own direction. nextCursor: null marks the last page. prevCursor pages backward.

Endpoint reference

Section titled “Endpoint reference”

List CI pipeline executions

Section titled “List CI pipeline executions”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/cipes

List the workspace’s CI pipeline executions (CIPEs), newest first by default. In-progress CIPEs are included (status NOT_STARTED or IN_PROGRESS): fields that are not final yet, such as completedAt, are absent, the runGroups summary (total, statusCounts) counts the run groups the CIPE has so far, and links.runGroups lists them. Filter by branch, statuses, a createdAt window, or run-group ciExecutionEnvs. cancellationRequest is optional. To investigate a CANCELED status, follow links.runGroups, open the canceled run groups, and inspect their workflow and run links. A CIPE whose self-healing work was skipped carries selfHealingSkip (reason, message, recordedAt). links.selfHealingFixes lists the fixes it has.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

branch

query

string

Match the CIPE branch, its VCS context branch, or its VCS context ref. A pull request’s CIPE is found both by the git branch name and by the branch its CI reported, often the pull request number.

statuses

query

string[]

Select statuses. Omit to include every CIPE, in-progress ones included. Values are case-insensitive. Repeat the key to select multiple values. Example: ["NOT_STARTED"]. Items: Allowed: NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELED, TIMED_OUT. Example: "NOT_STARTED". Exploded values.

createdAfter

query

string (date-time)

Inclusive lower bound on the CI pipeline execution’s createdAt. Supply an ISO-8601 timestamp with a timezone. Example: "2026-06-30T12:00:00Z".

createdBefore

query

string (date-time)

Inclusive upper bound on the CI pipeline execution’s createdAt. Supply an ISO-8601 timestamp with a timezone. Must not precede createdAfter. Example: "2026-06-30T12:00:00Z".

ciExecutionEnvs

query

string[]

Match CIPEs with at least one run group in a selected CI execution environment. Repeat the key to select multiple values. Exploded values.

limit

query

integer (int32)

Rows per page, 1..500 (default 100). Default: 100. minimum: 1. maximum: 500. Example: 100.

cursor

query

string

Opaque cursor from a previous page’s nextCursor/prevCursor.

sort

query

string

ASC or DESC (default), case-insensitive. First request only; a cursor carries its own direction and sort. Allowed: ASC, DESC. Default: "DESC". Example: "DESC".
Response body 200 OK

A page of CIPEs ordered by createdAt per the request’s sort.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: PageResponse_CipeResponse.

Example response

View field definitions

Response headers: RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

Other response codes: 400401429503

Get a CI pipeline execution

Section titled “Get a CI pipeline execution”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/cipes/{cipeId}

Fetch one terminal CIPE by id. Same shape as a list item, including the runGroups summary and the links map. An in-progress CIPE returns 409 with links.runGroups; it appears in the CIPE list while it runs. cancellationRequest is optional. To investigate a CANCELED status, follow links.runGroups, open the canceled run groups, and inspect their workflow and run links.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

cipeId

required

path

string

The CI pipeline execution’s id: 24 hexadecimal characters, not ciExecutionId.
Response body 200 OK

The CIPE.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: CipeResponse.

Example response

View field definitions

Response headers: RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

Other response codes: 400401404409429503

List run groups

Section titled “List run groups”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/run-groups

List run groups for the workspace. The list uses the parent CIPE’s createdAt. The newest CIPE is first by default. Run groups from one CIPE stay together. Filter by branch, ciExecutionEnv, cipeId, statuses, or a createdAfter/createdBefore window. A cipeId page for an in-progress CIPE holds the run groups it has so far; the list is complete once the CIPE’s status is terminal.

In-progress run groups are included (status NOT_STARTED or IN_PROGRESS): fields that are not final yet are absent, and links.runs lists the runs that have finished. List items contain run-group data. For a terminal run group, follow links.self for run and workflow information.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

branch

query

string

Match the parent CIPE’s branch, VCS context branch, or VCS context ref. A pull request’s run groups are found both by the git branch name and by the branch its CI reported, often the pull request number.

ciExecutionEnv

query

string

Match the CI execution environment name.

cipeId

query

string

Select a parent CI pipeline execution by its id: 24 hexadecimal characters, not ciExecutionId. An unknown parent returns 404. An in-progress CIPE lists the run groups it has so far, and more can follow: the list is complete once the CIPE’s status is terminal.

statuses

query

string[]

Select run-group statuses. Omit to include every status, in-progress run groups included. Values are case-insensitive. Repeat the key to select multiple values. Example: ["NOT_STARTED"]. Items: Allowed: NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELED, TIMED_OUT. Example: "NOT_STARTED". Exploded values.

createdAfter

query

string (date-time)

Inclusive lower bound on the parent CIPE’s createdAt, not the run group’s. Supply an ISO-8601 timestamp with a timezone. Example: "2026-06-30T12:00:00Z".

createdBefore

query

string (date-time)

Inclusive upper bound on the parent CIPE’s createdAt, not the run group’s. Supply an ISO-8601 timestamp with a timezone. Must not precede createdAfter. Example: "2026-06-30T12:00:00Z".

limit

query

integer (int32)

Rows per page, 1..500 (default 100). Default: 100. minimum: 1. maximum: 500. Example: 100.

cursor

query

string

Opaque cursor from a previous page’s nextCursor/prevCursor.

sort

query

string

ASC or DESC (default), case-insensitive. First request only; a cursor carries its own direction and sort. Allowed: ASC, DESC. Default: "DESC". Example: "DESC".
Response body 200 OK

A page of run groups ordered by the parent CIPE’s createdAt.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: PageResponse_RunGroupListResponse.

Example response

View field definitions

Response headers: RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

Other response codes: 400401404429503

Get a run group

Section titled “Get a run group”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/run-groups/{runGroupId}

Fetch one terminal run group by its id. URL-encode the id in the path. The response includes run information and optional workflow information. An in-progress run group returns 409 with links.runs; it appears in the run-group list while it runs.

workflow describes the Nx managed agent workflow for the run group. It includes its type, status, estimated credits, and summaries for steps, agents, and workflow instances. Follow its links to list these resources. workflow is null when the run group has no Nx managed agent workflow.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

runGroupId

required

path

string

The run group’s id, not cipeId. URL-encode the returned value as one path segment.
Response body 200 OK

The run group with its run summary and optional Nx managed agent workflow.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: RunGroupResponse.

Example response

View field definitions

Response headers: RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

Other response codes: 400401404409429503

List a run group's workflow steps

Section titled “List a run group&#39;s workflow steps”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/run-groups/{runGroupId}/steps

List the steps of the run group’s Nx managed agent workflow. A step runs across the workflow’s agents. Follow links.instances to list the workflow instances for that step. The link selects related rows from the run-group instance collection. Steps are in position order, with the last step first by default. Filter by execution statuses, launchTemplate, groupName, or parallel.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

runGroupId

required

path

string

The run group’s id, as returned by the run-groups API. URL-encode it as one path segment.

statuses

query

string[]

Select workflow execution statuses. Values are case-insensitive. Repeat the key to select multiple values. Example: ["UNKNOWN"]. Items: Allowed: UNKNOWN, NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELED, TIMED_OUT, MACHINE_TERMINATED, SKIPPED. Example: "UNKNOWN". Exploded values.

launchTemplate

query

string

Match the launch-template name.

groupName

query

string

Match the recorded workflow step group.

parallel

query

boolean

True selects parallel steps; false selects sequential steps. Omit to include both. Example: true.

limit

query

integer (int32)

Rows per page, 1..500 (default 100). Default: 100. minimum: 1. maximum: 500. Example: 100.

cursor

query

string

Opaque cursor from a previous page’s nextCursor/prevCursor.

sort

query

string

ASC or DESC (default), case-insensitive. First request only; a cursor carries its own direction and sort. Allowed: ASC, DESC. Default: "DESC". Example: "DESC".
Response body 200 OK

A page of workflow steps ordered by position.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: PageResponse_StepResponse.

Example response

View field definitions

Response headers: RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

Other response codes: 400401404409429503

Get a run-group workflow step

Section titled “Get a run-group workflow step”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/run-groups/{runGroupId}/steps/{stepId}

List a run group's workflow instances

Section titled “List a run group&#39;s workflow instances”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/run-groups/{runGroupId}/instances

List the workflow instances for a run group. Each instance is one step run on one Nx managed agent. BYOC agents do not have workflow instances. Use stepId to select one step across agents. Use agentName to select one agent across steps. Use both parameters to select one workflow instance.

These collection views use one pagination and filter model. Path parameters identify one resource. Query parameters select a related subset of this collection. Follow response links. Do not construct URLs from IDs.

Narrow the result by statuses, a startedAfter/startedBefore window, or restarted.

Each row represents one workflow step on one agent, not one agent boot. Agent restarts share a row; restartAttempts counts superseded executions. Each row includes the selected execution’s step, agent, status, times, and an available logs asset. Follow links.self for resourceUsage, terminationStatuses, timeoutInfo, and priorRuns. When links.agent exists, it identifies the Nx managed agent that ran the step. Older executions can lack agentName; their links.self still provides the instance address. Missing start times remain absent in responses, but use 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z for date filtering and sorting.

The selected execution has the latest start time, unless a restart boot selected in an earlier workflow step remains available for this step. Start-time ties use the last recorded execution. The other executions appear in priorRuns, sorted by start time then name in ascending order; they can start after the selected execution. Selection does not depend on the list’s sort direction.

List a run's tasks

Section titled “List a run&#39;s tasks”

Narrow by taskId, statuses, projectName, target, cacheStatus, agentName (DTE runs only), retried (true = only tasks with a prior attempt, false = only tasks that never retried), or a startedAt window. Task statuses are UNKNOWN, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELED, NOT_STARTED, DEPENDENCIES_FAILED, NOT_EXECUTABLE, TIMED_OUT, and SCHEDULED_IMPLICITLY. Each task can expose terminal output, a cache artifact, and an Ultracache report (asset type sandbox-report) in assets. A cache artifact is present only after upload or cache replay. A task that stopped before completion can have null startedAt, completedAt, cacheStatus, or hash fields. The params field can be an empty string. The links map gives the task and its parent run.

List daily task statistics

Section titled “List daily task statistics”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/task-stats

List daily task statistics for the workspace. Each row groups tasks by Nx project, target, target group, and CI or local execution for one UTC day based on run creation time. Only cache-enabled runs contribute; continuous tasks and nx-cloud start-agent runs are excluded. Cache and exit-code ratios use totalCount as their denominator and are fractions from 0 to 1. A target filter requires projectName. dateAfter and dateBefore accept an ISO-8601 date (2026-06-30) or timestamp and bound inclusive whole UTC days: a timestamp bounds the UTC day that contains it. Repeat percentiles with up to five unique integers from 0 to 100. For example, use percentiles=50&percentiles=95 to request P50 and P95. Each percentile is an approximate successful cache-miss duration in milliseconds; negative durations are excluded. Do not average row percentiles to calculate an overall percentile. The response omits durationPercentiles when no percentiles are requested. A percentile’s cacheMissMs is null when available duration data is insufficient; null is not zero and does not prove that no cache misses occurred.

List flaky-task metrics

Section titled “List flaky-task metrics”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/flaky-tasks

List daily flaky-task metric windows for the workspace. Each window groups CI cache-miss observations by Nx project, target, configuration, and cacheability. CI runs can contribute with or without distributed execution; local runs do not. Here, success means exit code 0, and failure means any nonzero exit code. flakinessRate is the fraction of successful observations whose task input hash also has failures within the same window. sampleSizeFlakinessRate counts all successful cache-miss observations and is the denominator, not the number of runs. Windows without successful observations are excluded. Zero-rate windows can appear unless minFlakinessRate excludes them. deflakedAutomatically counts each task input hash once per Nx execution with both successful and failed cache-miss attempts; it does not establish attempt order or a successful final attempt. Attempts without an execution identifier can also contribute and do not confirm a shared execution. A target filter requires project. A configuration filter requires project and target. windowStartAfter and windowEndBefore accept an ISO-8601 date (2026-06-30) or timestamp and bound inclusive whole UTC days. The current UTC day’s values can change until the day ends; set windowEndBefore to the previous UTC day to exclude today’s window. Use links.executions to access the paginated contributing distributed executions for each metric, not only those with mixed results. Observations without an execution identifier can affect metrics, but do not appear in the executions list.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

project

query

string

Match the Nx project name.

target

query

string

Match the Nx target name. Requires project.

configuration

query

string

Match the Nx target configuration. Requires both project and target.

isCacheable

query

boolean

Select metric windows for tasks marked cacheable (true) or non-cacheable (false). Omit to include both and windows with unknown cacheability. Example: true.

windowStartAfter

query

string (date) or string (date-time)

Inclusive first UTC day. Accepts an ISO-8601 date or timestamp; timestamps select their containing UTC day. Example: "2026-06-30".

windowEndBefore

query

string (date) or string (date-time)

Inclusive last UTC day. Accepts an ISO-8601 date or timestamp. Use the previous UTC day to exclude today’s mutable window. Example: "2026-06-30".

minFlakinessRate

query

number (double)

Inclusive minimum flakinessRate, as a fraction from 0 to 1. Omit or use 0 to include zero-rate windows with successful cache-miss observations. minimum: 0. maximum: 1.

limit

query

integer (int32)

Rows per page, 1..500 (default 100). Default: 100. minimum: 1. maximum: 500. Example: 100.

cursor

query

string

Opaque cursor from a previous page’s nextCursor/prevCursor.

sort

query

string

ASC or DESC (default), case-insensitive. First request only; a cursor carries its own direction and sort. Allowed: ASC, DESC. Default: "DESC". Example: "DESC".

List Self-Healing fixes

Section titled “List Self-Healing fixes”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/self-healing-fixes

List the Self-Healing CI fix records of one CI pipeline execution (cipeId) or one run group (runGroup). One of the two filters is required. A pipeline normally has at most one fix, created for one of its run groups. A fix is listed as soon as it is created, while its pipeline may still be running, and it keeps changing after the pipeline finishes: suggestedFixStatus follows the generation of the change, verificationStatus the re-run of tasks with the change applied, and userAction what was done with it. An empty page means no fix was created; the CIPE’s selfHealingSkip says why when that was recorded. List items never carry the patch (suggestedFix); fetch a fix by id for it.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

cipeId

query

string

Select the fixes of one CI pipeline execution by its id: 24 hexadecimal characters, not ciExecutionId. An unknown CIPE returns 404. Fixes recorded without a CIPE id are not matched; select those with runGroup.

runGroup

query

string

Select the fixes of one run group by its id. An unknown run group returns 404.

limit

query

integer (int32)

Rows per page, 1..500 (default 100). Default: 100. minimum: 1. maximum: 500. Example: 100.

cursor

query

string

Opaque cursor from a previous page’s nextCursor/prevCursor.

sort

query

string

ASC or DESC (default), case-insensitive. First request only; a cursor carries its own direction and sort. Allowed: ASC, DESC. Default: "DESC". Example: "DESC".
Response body 200 OK

A page of fixes ordered by createdAt per the request’s sort.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: PageResponse_SelfHealingFixResponse.

Example response

View field definitions

Response headers: RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

Other response codes: 400401404429503

Get a Self-Healing fix

Section titled “Get a Self-Healing fix”

GET /nx-cloud/data/v1/self-healing-fixes/{fixId}

Fetch one Self-Healing CI fix by id, in any state. Same shape as a list item, plus the patch in suggestedFix once a change has been suggested.

Parameters

NameLocationTypeDescription

fixId

required

path

string

The fix’s id: 24 hexadecimal characters, returned as id by listSelfHealingFixes.
Response body 200 OK

The fix.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: SelfHealingFixResponse.

Example response

View field definitions

Response headers: RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

Other response codes: 400401404429503

HTTP response codes

Section titled “HTTP response codes”

400 Bad Request

Section titled “400 Bad Request”

  • Invalid limit, cursor, timestamp, date range, or status.

  • A path parameter was malformed or invalid for this entity’s id format.

  • Invalid limit, cursor, cipeId, status, or createdAt window.

  • Invalid limit, cursor, or filter.

  • An unknown asset type, or a malformed path/query parameter.

  • Invalid limit, cursor, status, filter, or createdAt window.

  • Invalid limit, cursor, status, or startedAt window.

  • Invalid limit, cursor, filter combination, or date window.

  • Invalid limit, cursor, filter combination, rate, or window.

  • Invalid metric id, limit, or cursor.

  • Neither cipeId nor runGroup was given, or an invalid id, limit or cursor.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: ErrorResponse.

View field definitions

401 Unauthorized

Section titled “401 Unauthorized”

  • The credentials are missing or invalid, or the request uses an unsupported access method. Authentication failures return plain text. Authorization failures return a JSON error body.

404 Not Found

Section titled “404 Not Found”

  • No CIPE with that id in this workspace.

  • No CIPE with the filtered cipeId in this workspace.

  • No run group with that id in this workspace.

  • No such run group or Nx managed agent workflow.

  • No such run group, workflow, or step.

  • No such run group, workflow, step, or Nx managed agent.

  • No such run group, workflow, or instance.

  • No such run group, workflow, instance, prior run, or log location.

  • No such run group in this workspace.

  • No such run group or agent.

  • No such run group or agent, no prior boot at that boot index, or the selected record has no report.

  • No run group with the filtered runGroup id in this workspace.

  • No run with that id in this workspace.

  • No such run, or no task with that id (and batchId, if given) in the run.

  • No such run or task, or the task has no asset of that type.

  • No such flaky-task metric in the workspace.

  • No CIPE or run group with that id in this workspace.

  • No fix with that id in this workspace.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: ErrorResponse.

View field definitions

409 Conflict

Section titled “409 Conflict”

  • The CIPE is still running (entityStatus NOT_STARTED or IN_PROGRESS). links.runGroups lists its run groups so far, running ones included.

  • The run group or its linked workflow is still running. links.runs lists the run group’s finished runs.

  • The run group or its Nx managed agent workflow is still running; steps, instances and agents are served once both finish. links.runs lists the run group’s finished runs.

  • The run is in a non-terminal state (in-progress); only terminal runs are queryable. Retry once it finishes.

  • The run or task is in a non-terminal state (in-progress); only terminal entities are queryable. Retry once it finishes.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: NotTerminalErrorResponse.

View field definitions

429 Too Many Requests

Section titled “429 Too Many Requests”

  • The organization’s Nx Cloud Public API quota is exhausted (rate_limit_exceeded). Every workspace and access token in the organization shares one quota, and each request costs one unit. By default, Free organizations get 30 requests/minute with bursts of up to 10. Team, Pro, and OSS organizations get 60 requests/minute with bursts of up to 10. Enterprise organizations get 2500 requests/minute with bursts of up to 500. The global API rate limit can also return 429, with an empty body. Wait Retry-After seconds before retrying.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: ErrorResponse.

View field definitions

Response headers: Retry-After, RateLimit-Policy, RateLimit.

503 Service Unavailable

Section titled “503 Service Unavailable”

  • The Nx Cloud Public API is temporarily at capacity (data_api_at_capacity), could not complete the request in time (query_deadline_exceeded), could not persist its required audit record (audit_log_unavailable), or could not check the organization’s quota (rate_limit_unavailable). No data is returned. Retry per the Retry-After header.

Content type: application/json.

Schema: ErrorResponse.

View field definitions

Response headers: Retry-After.

Response headers

Section titled “Response headers”

RateLimit-Policy

Section titled “RateLimit-Policy”

Type: string.

Documented with HTTP 200, 302, 429.

The organization’s quota: q requests per w seconds, for example "organization";q=10;w=10.

RateLimit

Section titled “RateLimit”

Type: string.

Documented with HTTP 200, 302, 429.

r requests remain now, and the quota is full again in t seconds, for example "organization";r=7;t=3.

Retry-After

Section titled “Retry-After”

Type: string.

Documented with HTTP 429.

Seconds until the next request is allowed.

Documented with HTTP 503.

Minimum seconds to wait before retrying (server-randomized). Treat it as a floor and apply exponential backoff on repeated 503s.

Schema and field definitions

Section titled “Schema and field definitions”

CipeResponse

Section titled “CipeResponse”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

id

required

string

The CI pipeline execution identifier: 24 hexadecimal characters. Use this id in CIPE paths and cipeId filters, not ciExecutionId.

status

required

string

The pipeline status: NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELED or TIMED_OUT.

createdAt

required

string (date-time)

The pipeline creation time, in UTC.

updatedAt

null or string (date-time)

The last recorded update time, in UTC; absent when unavailable.

completedAt

null or string (date-time)

The recorded completion time, in UTC; absent when unavailable, even for a terminal pipeline.

workspaceId

required

string

The workspace identifier: 24 hexadecimal characters. It identifies the workspace that owns this CI pipeline execution.

ciExecutionId

required

string

The execution identifier supplied by the CI integration. Use id, not this value, in CIPE paths and cipeId filters.

branch

null or string

The recorded branch name; absent when not supplied.

vcsContext

null or VcsContextResponse

Recorded version-control metadata; absent when not supplied.

cancellationRequest

null or CipeCancellationRequestResponse

The recognized cancellation request, if recorded. Its absence does not prove that no cancellation occurred.

selfHealingSkip

null or SelfHealingSkipResponse

Why self-healing work was skipped, if recorded.

runGroups

required

ChildCollectionSummary

Counts for all related run groups without optional filters. While the CIPE runs, the counts are the run groups it has so far and can still change. Follow links.runGroups for their records.

links

required

Dictionary of string

Relative GET URLs: self addresses this CIPE; runGroups lists its run groups; selfHealingFixes lists its Self-Healing fixes, which is an empty page when it has none. While the CIPE runs, self returns 409 and runGroups lists the run groups it has so far, running ones included.

AgentResponse

Section titled “AgentResponse”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

name

required

string

The agent name used in paths. Nx managed restarts share one identity. BYOC uses its display name, or instanceName when no display name exists, so restarts can have different names. URL-encode name as one path segment.

status

required

string

OFFLINE when an offline time exists; otherwise ONLINE. This describes the selected boot’s recorded times, not a live probe.

instanceName

required

string

The selected boot’s full instance name. The endpoint description explains boot selection. Use name, not instanceName, to address the agent.

launchTemplate

null or string

The recorded launch-template name; absent when unavailable.

cpuCores

null or integer (int64)

The reported CPU core count; absent when system information is unavailable.

totalMemory

null or integer (int64)

The reported total system memory, in bytes; absent when system information is unavailable.

onlineAt

null or string (date-time)

The selected boot’s online time, in UTC; absent when unavailable. Agent list ordering uses 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z for missing times and follows the requested sort direction.

offlineAt

null or string (date-time)

The recorded boot offline time, in UTC; absent when no offline time exists.

avgCpu

null or number (double)

The average sampled CPU usage across cores, in percent (100 per full core); absent when metrics are unavailable.

maxCpu

null or number (double)

The maximum sampled CPU usage across cores, in percent (100 per full core); absent when metrics are unavailable.

avgMemory

null or number (double)

The average sampled memory usage, in bytes; absent when metrics are unavailable.

maxMemory

null or number (double)

The maximum sampled memory usage, in bytes; absent when metrics are unavailable.

instances

required

InstanceCollectionSummary

Counts for this agent’s workflow instances (one step on this agent) and restarts. Empty for an agent without a workflow, including BYOC.

assets

required

DataAsset[]

Resource-utilization asset API URLs for the selected boot. Follow each URL for a signed download redirect.

priorBoots

AgentBootResponse[]

Earlier boots, oldest first. Zero-based array positions select the asset boot query parameter. Omit boot to select the current response’s boot.

links

required

Dictionary of string

OFFLINE when an offline time exists; otherwise ONLINE. This describes the earlier boot’s recorded times, not a live probe.

maxCpu

avgMemory

maxMemory

null or number (double)

Section titled “TaskCollectionSummary”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

total

required

integer (int32)

The number of final task records before optional filters, not the number of attempts. Batch variants can share a task id.

statusCounts

required

Dictionary of integer (int32)

Final task counts keyed by public status. Statuses with no tasks are absent. Counts sum to total.

retried

required

integer (int32)

The number of task records with at least one prior failed attempt, not the number of attempts.

retryAttempts

required

integer (int32)

The total number of prior failed attempts across task records, excluding their final attempts.

retriedStatusCounts

required

Dictionary of integer (int32)

Final status counts for retried task records only. Statuses with no retried tasks are absent. Counts sum to retried.

TaskResponse

Section titled “TaskResponse”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

id

required

string

The Nx task id in project:target[:configuration] form, such as myapp:build. URL-encode it as one path segment. Use batchId to distinguish variants within a run.

status

required

TaskStatus

The task’s final status, including tasks that could not start or execute.

startedAt

null or string (date-time)

The recorded task start time, in UTC; absent when unavailable.

completedAt

null or string (date-time)

The recorded task completion time, in UTC; absent when unavailable.

projectName

required

string

The Nx project name.

target

required

string

The Nx target name.

targetGroupName

null or string

The recorded target group name; absent when unavailable.

configuration

null or string

The Nx target configuration; absent when not specified.

params

required

string

The recorded task parameters. An empty string means no parameters were recorded.

cacheStatus

required

null or string

The recorded cache result. Null when the task stopped before it produced a cache result.

hash

required

null or string

The Nx computation hash, not the task identifier. Use it to compare computations. Null when the task stopped before hashing completed.

continuous

required

boolean

Whether Nx configured the task to run continuously.

cacheable

required

boolean

Whether the task was eligible for caching; this does not mean it used a cached result.

batchId

null or string

The batch identifier; absent for unbatched tasks. Supply it as the URL-encoded batchId query value to distinguish records with the same task id.

agentName

null or string

The assigned agent identity for a distributed run (DTE); absent for non-DTE runs and unassigned tasks.

assets

required

DataAsset[]

Asset API URLs for this attempt. Follow each URL to resolve a time-limited download redirect.

priorAttempts

TaskAttemptResponse[]

Failed attempts before the final attempt, oldest first. Zero-based array positions select the asset attempt query parameter for logs.

links

required

Dictionary of string

Relative GET URLs: self and run; cacheOrigin appears only when requested and available.

TaskStatResponse

Section titled “TaskStatResponse”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

date

required

string (date-time)

The UTC day at midnight, based on run creation time rather than task start time.

projectName

required

string

The Nx project name shared by the tasks in this row.

target

required

string

The Nx target name shared by the tasks in this row.

targetGroupName

null or string

The name of the project’s target group that contains this target. Different groups have separate rows; absent when unavailable.

isCI

required

boolean

Whether this row represents CI runs. Runs with a branch value count as CI; runs without one count as local.

totalCount

required

integer (int32)

The number of task entries represented by this row, including cache hits. Only cache-enabled runs contribute. Excludes continuous tasks and nx-cloud start-agent runs.

cacheStatusRatio

required

TaskStatCacheStatusRatio

Fractions of totalCount for each cache result. They can sum to less than 1 when entries have other or unavailable cache results.

averageDuration

required

TaskStatAverageDuration

Mean durations in milliseconds per cache category. Cache-miss means use successful executions only.

statusCodeRatio

required

TaskStatStatusCodeRatio

Exit-code fractions using totalCount as the denominator.

durationPercentiles

null or TaskStatDurationPercentile[]

Approximate duration percentiles in milliseconds for successful cache misses in this row. Absent when no percentiles were requested; individual estimates can be null.
Schema definition

TaskStatCacheStatusRatio

Section titled “TaskStatCacheStatusRatio”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

localCacheHit

required

number (double)

Local-cache-hit task entries divided by totalCount, as a fraction from 0 to 1. minimum: 0. maximum: 1.

remoteCacheHit

required

number (double)

Remote-cache-hit task entries divided by totalCount, as a fraction from 0 to 1. minimum: 0. maximum: 1.

cacheMiss

required

number (double)

Cache-miss task entries, successful or failed, divided by totalCount, as a fraction from 0 to 1. minimum: 0. maximum: 1.
Schema definition

TaskStatAverageDuration

Section titled “TaskStatAverageDuration”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

localCacheHitMs

required

number (double)

Total local-cache-hit duration in milliseconds divided by the local-cache-hit count. Zero when no local hits contribute or their total duration is zero.

remoteCacheHitMs

required

number (double)

Total remote-cache-hit duration in milliseconds divided by the remote-cache-hit count. Zero when no remote hits contribute or their total duration is zero.

cacheMissMs

required

number (double)

Total successful cache-miss duration in milliseconds divided by the successful-cache-miss count. Zero when no successful misses contribute or their total duration is zero.
Schema definition

TaskStatStatusCodeRatio

Section titled “TaskStatStatusCodeRatio”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

zero

required

number (double)

Task entries with exit code 0 divided by totalCount, as a fraction from 0 to 1. minimum: 0. maximum: 1.

nonZero

required

number (double)

Task entries whose exit code is not 0, including unavailable exit codes, divided by totalCount. Equals 1 minus zero; not a separate task status. minimum: 0. maximum: 1.
Schema definition

TaskStatDurationPercentile

Section titled “TaskStatDurationPercentile”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

percentile

required

integer (int32)

The requested percentile rank, from 0 to 100; 50 is the median and 95 is P95. minimum: 0. maximum: 100.

cacheMissMs

required

null or number (double)

Approximate duration in milliseconds at the requested percentile for successful cache misses with nonnegative durations. Null means insufficient available duration data, not zero duration or proof that no cache misses occurred.

FlakyTaskResponse

Section titled “FlakyTaskResponse”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

id

required

string

The metric’s 24-character hexadecimal public identifier. Use it as metricId to list contributing executions.

project

required

string

The Nx project name for this window.

target

required

string

The Nx target name for this window.

configuration

null or string

The Nx target configuration shared by this window’s observations; absent when not specified. Different configurations have separate metric windows.

windowStart

required

string (date-time)

The inclusive window start at UTC midnight. Observations use task start times.

windowEnd

required

string (date-time)

The exclusive window end at the next UTC midnight. Today’s window changes until it ends.

flakinessRate

required

number (double)

Successful cache-miss observations for input hashes that have both successes and failures within this window, divided by all successful cache-miss observations. A fraction from 0 to 1, not a percentage or the fraction of failed attempts. minimum: 0. maximum: 1.

sampleSizeFlakinessRate

required

integer (int32)

The denominator of flakinessRate: all successful cache-miss observations, not all attempts or unique runs. Use it to assess the amount of data behind the rate.

totalReruns

required

integer (int32)

The number of cache-miss observations beyond the first for each task input hash in this window. Includes hashes with no mixed results. Not the number of runs that retried.

deflakedAutomatically

required

integer (int32)

Counts a task input hash once per Nx execution if it has both successful and failed cache-miss attempts. One execution can count for multiple hashes. Does not establish attempt order or a successful final attempt. Attempts without an execution identifier can also contribute; they do not confirm a shared execution.

isCacheable

null or boolean

Whether Nx marked this window’s tasks as cacheable. True, false, and unknown values have separate metric windows; absent means unknown, not false.

links

required

FlakyTaskLinksResponse

GET URLs for this metric’s related data.
Schema definition

FlakyTaskLinksResponse

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

executions

required

string

The relative GET URL for paginated contributing distributed executions, not only mixed-result executions. Observations without an execution identifier affect metrics but do not appear in this list.

SelfHealingFixResponse

Section titled “SelfHealingFixResponse”

Type: object.

PropertyTypeDescription

id

required

string

The fix identifier: 24 hexadecimal characters.

createdAt

required

string (date-time)

When the fix record was created, in UTC.

updatedAt

null or string (date-time)

The last recorded update time, in UTC; absent when the record was never updated.

cipeId

null or string

The CI pipeline execution the fix belongs to; absent on records stored without it.

ciExecutionId

required

string

The execution identifier supplied by the CI integration.

runGroup

required

string

The id of the run group whose failed tasks the fix was created for.

suggestedFixStatus

required

string

The state of fix generation: NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED, TIMED_OUT or CANCELED.

suggestedFixFailureReason

null or string

Why fix generation failed, when recorded.

suggestedFixFailureReasonType

null or string

The recorded category of the generation failure, when recorded.

verificationStatus

required

string

The state of verifying the fix by re-running tasks with it applied: NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED, TIMED_OUT or CANCELED.

failureClassification

null or string

How the failure was classified: code_change, environment_state or flaky_task; absent until classified.

suggestedFixDescription

null or string

A short description of the suggested change; absent until one is suggested.

suggestedFixReasoning

null or string

The reasoning recorded with the suggested change; absent until one is suggested.

confidence

null or integer (int32)

The recorded confidence in the fix, when recorded.

confidenceReasoning

null or string

The reasoning behind the recorded confidence, when recorded.

suggestedFix

null or string

The suggested change as a git patch. Returned when a fix is fetched by id; never present in a list.

suggestedAt

null or string (date-time)

When the change was suggested, in UTC.

verifiedAt

null or string (date-time)

When verification finished, in UTC.

userAction

required

string

What was done with the fix: NONE, APPLIED, REJECTED, APPLIED_LOCALLY, APPLIED_AUTOMATICALLY, REVERTED or RERUN_REQUESTED.

userActionOrigin

null or string

Where the action came from: NX_CLOUD_APP, NX_CONSOLE_VSCODE, NX_CONSOLE_INTELLIJ, NX_CLI, VCS_COMMENT or NX_MCP; absent when no action was recorded.

userActionRecordedAt

null or string (date-time)

When the action was recorded, in UTC.

commitSha

null or string

The commit that applied the fix to the branch, when recorded.

fixApplicationAttempts

SelfHealingFixApplicationAttemptResponse[]

The recorded attempts to apply the fix, oldest first.

autoApplySkipped

null or boolean

Whether applying the fix automatically was skipped; absent when not recorded.

autoApplySkipReason

null or string

Why applying the fix automatically was skipped, when recorded.

autoAppliedTasks

null or string[]

The ids of the tasks whose fix was applied automatically, when recorded.

flakyRerunPending

null or boolean

Whether a rerun of a flaky failure is waiting for the pipeline to finish; absent when not recorded. A rerun is an empty commit pushed to the branch.

flakyRerunSkipped

null or boolean

Whether the rerun of a flaky failure was skipped because the branch reached its rerun limit; absent when not recorded.

branchIsOutdated

required

boolean

Whether the branch has moved on since the fix was created, so the fix no longer applies to its head.

fixTasks

SelfHealingFixTaskResponse[]

The failed tasks the fix was created for.

fixedTasks

string[]

The ids of the tasks the suggested change is meant to fix.

otherFailedTasks

null or string[]

The ids of failed tasks the suggested change does not address, when recorded.

verificationTasksExecuted

null or string[]

The ids of the tasks re-run to verify the fix, when recorded.

remoteTaskSummary

null or string

A summary of the failing tasks’ output from CI, when recorded.

localTaskSummary

null or string

A summary of the tasks’ output from the fix’s own run, when recorded.

shortLink

null or string

The short code that identifies this fix to nx-cloud apply-locally; absent until a change is suggested.

links

required

Dictionary of string

Relative GET URLs: self addresses this fix, with its patch; runGroup and cipe address its parents. cipe is absent on records stored without a CIPE id.
